description:
pkix-identity/src/lib.rs:706-708 explicitly documents that IPv4-in-IPv6 forms like '::ffff:192.0.2.1' are not supported, with the rationale 'a future extension can add this without API change'.

Impact: real-world TLS configs sometimes use IPv4-mapped forms in operator-facing config; if a target string comes from such config and the cert SAN holds the canonical 16-byte form, the match will fail with MalformedInput rather than NoMatchingSan. Not a security bug (fails closed) but a UX cliff.

There is no integration test or rustdoc-level note in ServerName::ip_address advertising this limitation publicly. The crate's Limitations section in the module doc doesn't mention it.

Action: either
(a) add a public Limitations bullet ('IPv4-mapped IPv6 like ::ffff:1.2.3.4 not parsed; pass the IPv4 string instead') so users see it in rustdoc, or
(b) implement the parse path (small — detect 'final group with dots', parse as IPv4, slot into bytes 12-15). pyca/cryptography handles this.
title: IPv4-mapped/embedded IPv6 (::ffff:1.2.3.4) not parseable; documented limitation but no test
